Those bosses include Dario Amodei of Anthropic, which owns Claude; his rival Sam Altman of OpenAI, which owns ChatGPT and its descendants; and their competitor, SpaceX founder Elon Musk, who owns Grok. The debate has raged around the world for the past few days. Dividing the world into two kinds of people never works, so we’ll go with three: this issue has divided the world into those who agree that AI may indeed kill us all, those who think Musk et al are out to fool us all, and those in the “don’t know/can’t say” camp. Our analysis leads us to think there ought to be a fourth camp: those who agree that the AI bosses may be trying to fool us all, and also that AI may kill us all. The two are not mutually exclusive. Debates over AI safety are old, but the latest drama began with the public resignation of Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher at Anthropic who had earlier worked at OpenAI. In a viral tweet , Coxon, who worked on training AI models, wrote that both companies are “racing straight to superintelligence and gambling with our lives…Do not underestimate the power of this technology. items.title: The science on trans athletes is inconclusive. Cricket’s prejudice isn’t
items.summary: If cricket fans across the eras are to be believed, the game has always been on the brink of extinction. The game should have died yesterday; somehow it survived today, but tomorrow it will definitely slip into oblivion. The unintended consequence of this perpetual mode of apprehension is that on days when there are no real obstacles to overcome and no real issues to solve, imaginary problems must be conjured up, solely because the fight must go on; the chatter machine must keep ticking. Last month, attention fell on women’s cricket, and this purportedly novel effort to ‘save’ it brought in droves of commentators, cricketers, and even those who have always justified its marginal status by claiming it can’t generate more revenue. Everyone came in unison to protect the sanctity of women’s cricket from what they believed, and want us to believe, is the biggest threat to its existence: the possibility of trans athletes competing in women’s sports. This war was waged in the wake of the latest development surrounding Anaya Bangar, a transgender cricketer from India, also the daughter of former Indian cricketer Sanjay Bangar. This was after she received a nod from Cricket Australia (CA) to play elite-level women’s cricket, which would eventually make her eligible to play in the Big Bash League (BBL), Australia's premier T20 competition, next year. One would expect such unchecked fury to be saved for raging against the actual issues like underfunding, pay disparity, and other systemic hurdles that are plaguing the women’s sport. Yet, these roadblocks never attain the same immediacy. What, then, explains the hysteria around the possibility of a trans woman playing in women’s sport? For the self-anointed saviours of women’s cricket, this became a fight to preserve the ‘sanctity’ of the game by resisting the entry of trans women, who according to them are here to colonise the game with their brute strength and push out the cisgender athlete to extinction, even though evidence at hand fails to support this fictitious panic. To date, Danielle McGahey remains the only transgender athlete to play international cricket, representing Canada's women's team in six matches. She had to retire after the International Cricket Council (ICC) imposed a blanket ban on transgender cricketers who have undergone male puberty from women's cricket. items.title: How deficient rainfall is affecting ragi farmers in Karnataka’s Mandya
items.summary: Shiva Shekhar, a 40-year-old farmer from Padavalapatna village in Mandya district's Nagamangala taluk, could not sow ragi this kharif. “I kept waiting for the rain but it never came, so I sowed cowpea instead, which is more drought-tolerant,” he said on September 16. Karnataka is the largest ragi-producing state in the country. In 2025-26, India produced 2 million tonnes of ragi, of which 1.47 million tonnes came from Karnataka, according to the Third Advance Estimates for the year from the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. The state also accounted for about 73% of the area under ragi that year, at 979,000 hectares. Of that, Mandya—located about 40 km north of Mysuru—accounted for about 53,300 hectares. Broadly, ragi sowing at the national and state levels has kept pace with last year. But in Mandya, against a target of 63,385 hectare for this year, ragi was sown in 1,213 hectare (1.91%) by September 11, data shared by Jayaswamy, joint director of agriculture for Mandya, show . By September 11, Karnataka had an overall decline of 1.5 million hectares in kharif sowing area compared to last year. Of this, roughly a third each was in paddy, and the broad category of millets and coarse cereals. “The seasonal decline in Kharif millet acreage during low-rainfall years reflects practical, farm level adaptation rather than a loss of confidence in the crop,” said C. Tara Satyavathi, director of ICAR’s Indian Institute Of Millet Research. “When monsoon showers are delayed or substantially deficient, topsoil moisture drops below the threshold required for seed emergence,” explained Satyavathi. “If the mid-August window passes, sowing full-duration varieties can expose the crop to terminal moisture stress later in October-November.” For Shekhar, shifting to cowpea did not help either. “Due to the lack of rainfall and soil moisture, this crop [cowpea] is also drying up. There seems to be no chance of yield,” he said. “July had an 83% rainfall deficit and August a 70% deficit. In the last two months, we have hardly had even one rainy day in the district,” said Jayaswamy. items.title: BAPS: The Hindu organisation at the heart of Modi’s cultural diplomacy
items.summary: “Strike and closure of the Eiffel Tower after the expulsion of female staff during a visit by a Hindu delegation” This was what a prominent French newspaper said on September 7 this year. The Hindu delegation belonged to the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, or the BAPS, and it made global headlines. But the interesting question is not just what happened in Paris. It is this: how did a religious organisation with deeply conservative internal rules become one of the most powerful global faces of Indian culture? BAPS has spectacular temples, a wealthy and influential global following, a vast charity network and an extraordinary relationship with Narendra Modi. It also has a much more complicated history involving women, caste, labour and political power. So who exactly is BAPS? And why has the Indian state invested so heavily in projecting it worldwide? items.title: Suspended directors have to give confidentiality undertaking for access to resolution plan: NCLAT
items.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) has held that a resolution professional can ask suspended directors to furnish a confidentiality undertaking before providing them access to a resolution plan and other confidential material in a corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) [Mandava Prabhakar Rao Vs Navneet Gupta]. Technical Member Naresh Salecha , who was called upon to resolve an earlier split verdict by the NCLAT, agreed with the view that such a requirement does not violate the rights of suspended directors to participate CIRP. “ The resolution professional can take an undertaking from members of the erstwhile board of directors to maintain confidentiality, ” Salecha held. He said that the right of suspended directors to access resolution plans has to operate alongside their obligation to maintain confidentiality. The ruling arose from appeals filed by Mandava Prabhakar Rao, a suspended director of NSL Nagapatnam Power and Infratech Limited. The dispute concerned the company's 20th Committee of Creditors (CoC) meeting held on July 16, 2024. Rao had nominated Nelluri Bapuji to represent the suspended management in CoC meetings. Bapuji had participated in several earlier meetings. However, at the 20th meeting, he was asked to leave after failing to furnish a written authorisation and a confidentiality undertaking. The meeting involved consideration of resolution plans submitted for the company. Rao challenged Bapuji's exclusion, arguing that it deprived the suspended management of its statutory right to participate in the CIRP and access material necessary to make representations before the CoC. The resolution professional maintained that the 20th CoC meeting involved commercially sensitive material and that access could be granted only after compliance with confidentiality requirements. The appeals were initially heard by a two-member NCLAT Bench comprising Judicial Member Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma and Technical Member Jatindranath Swain. The Bench delivered a split verdict on November 10, 2025. Justice Sharma upheld the insolvency process while Swain took the view that the exclusion of the suspended director’s representative from the 20th CoC meeting was impermissible and warranted reopening the process from that stage. In view of the difference of opinion, the points on which the two members disagreed were referred to Technical Member Naresh Salecha for determination as the third member. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana also ordered the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or any other authority not to submit any report to the High Court in the meantime. The Bench also said that if any agency has knowledge of any disproportionate assets belonging to any individual, it can proceed on its own and the same does not require court orders. items.title: Karnataka cancels 16 licences, suspends 8 over spurious drugs: Full list
items.summary: The Karnataka Food Safety and Drugs Administration (FSDA) has cancelled the licences of 16 pharmaceutical retailers and wholesalers, and suspended those of eight others, including Pfizer Ltd’s wholesale depot in Nelamangala, as part of an ongoing investigation into the alleged distribution and sale of spurious drugs. The action follows the FSDA’s August 18 raid on a farmhouse in Bidadi, in Bengaluru South district, where the department said it uncovered an unlicensed drug repacking and relabelling operation. Drugs, injection-filling machinery, forged labels and stamps and other material worth Rs 5.05 crore were seized from the premises. As part of the follow-up investigation, the FSDA said it cancelled 16 drug licences and suspended eight others belonging to retailers and wholesalers involved in the alleged distribution and sale of the spurious medicines. The licence of Pfizer Ltd’s wholesale depot at Kempanalinganahalli in Nelamangala taluk, Bengaluru Rural district, has also been suspended. The 16 cancelled licences include those of Avesco Healthcare, Bangalore Speciality Pharma, Bengalurus Speciality Pharma, Patel Medi Trade, Rajarajeshwari Pharma, N.S. Pharma, Surya Speciality Pharma, SWS Pharma, Krupa Healthcare, St Philomena Hospital Drug Centre, Sagar Pharma, Zymus Pharma, Fortune Medical Solutions, Excelcare Pharma, Patel Medicals and another firm named Bangalore Speciality Pharma. The eight suspended licences are those of Med Pharma, Surya Speciality Hospital, Sagar Pharma’s Unit-II, Vivantha Pharmaceuticals, Maruthi Medicals, Viva Pharma, Hi-5 Pharma and Pfizer Ltd. According to the FSDA, the Bidadi premises were allegedly being used to procure low-cost medicines from neighbouring states, refill them into new vials and relabel them as expensive, imported life-saving drugs of multinational companies. The department said, “To deceive buyers and maximise illicit profits, the counterfeit labels featured QR/scanning codes, which were found to be completely nonfunctional upon verification. items.title: Cops Kanthi Rana, Vishal Gunni accused in Kadambari Jethwani case given new postings
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Two years after their suspension in the infamous Kadambari Jethwani case, the Andhra Pradesh government on Sunday, September 20, transferred and assigned new postings for former Vijayawada Commissioner Kanthi Rana Tata and Deputy Commissioner Vishal Gunni. The government issued orders posting Kanthi Rana as the Traffic Management and Road Safety’s Inspector General of Police. Vishal Gunni was posted as Deputy Inspector General of Police, Training, in the existing vacancy, and given full additional charge as Director of the Andhra Pradesh Police Academy (APPA) until further orders. The postings come two weeks after the Andhra government, on September 4, revoked their suspension. While revoking their suspension, the state government said that the decision was based on reports from the Director General of Police (DGP) and the Head of Police Force (HoPF). The two cops were accused of illegally confining and harassing Mumbai based actress Kadambari Jethwani and her family. Former DGP (Intelligence) Sitharama Anjaneyalu was accused of booking flights for Kanthi Rana and Vishal to Mumbai for the arrest of the actor without proper written instructions or due investigation. Kanthi Rana and Vishal Gunni were charged with acting solely on oral instructions and arresting the actress without due diligence. The officers were also accused of carrying out an arrest even before the registration of the First Information Report (FIR) which raises concerns of procedural lapses. Jethwani had complained to NTR Police Commissioner SV Rajasekhar Babu in August 2024 accusing YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) leader and movie producer KVR Vidyasagar of colluding with the officers and filing a case of extortion and forgery against her. Jethwani said that along with her, her parents were picked up from Mumbai to Vijayawada without any prior notice and further alleged that they were placed in judicial custody for over a month. items.title: Karnataka minister says ‘nothing wrong’ in tipping officials, sparks row
items.summary: Karnataka Excise Minister and Hassan district in-charge minister KM Shivalinge Gowda triggered a controversy on Saturday, September 19, after he said citizens could “respectfully” offer money to government officials who complete their work on time. Gowda made the remarks while addressing a ‘Praja Seva Andolana’ public grievance meeting in Sakleshpur, Hassan district. He was responding to a query from a member of the public when he said, “Whatever you want to offer, you can do so respectfully. It is your dharma, but nobody should take money forcibly.” When some people in the audience asked what they should offer “respectfully”, the minister reportedly said it was left to them. The minister had also said there was “nothing wrong” if citizens willingly gave ‘tips’ or an ‘honorarium’ to government officials for getting their work done on time. The remarks drew objections from people at the meeting. Punit, a farmer from Alur who was present with a land-related grievance, questioned the minister’s statement. “Officials are paid a salary. Why should we give them tips? Doesn’t this amount to encouraging bribery?” he asked. As more people joined the protest, the meeting reportedly witnessed chaos. Some of those objecting to the minister’s remarks were asked to stop arguing with him, while Gowda was also heard asking officials to send them out of the venue. The minister subsequently attempted to clarify his remarks. Gowda said he was trying to convey that officials should not forcibly collect money and that honest officials should be respected. “I only said that we should appreciate officials for their work; I never suggested giving them bribes,” the minister said. Gowda also clarified on Sunday, September 20, that his remarks had been misunderstood. “A person complained that bribe was being sought to get his work done. I told him not to give any money, but to respect the officer. My statement has been misunderstood,” he said. Hassan Deputy Commissioner KS Latha Kumari, who was present at the meeting, intervened as the situation became tense. She said, “The minister’s statement has been misinterpreted. If officials demand bribes for work, stringent legal action will be taken against them.” The Deputy Commissioner also said strict action would be taken against any official who demanded a bribe to discharge their duty. items.title: Actor-wrestler Saurav Gurjar remanded in sexual exploitation case
items.summary: Actor and former professional wrestler Saurav Gurjar was remanded to 14 days of judicial custody on Sunday, September 20, after Gachibowli police arrested him in connection with a woman’s complaint alleging sexual exploitation on the false promise of marriage. According to a The Hindu report , Gurjar was intercepted by immigration officials at Mumbai airport on the night of September 17 after arriving from the Middle East. A Look Out Circular (LOC) had been issued against him in connection with the case. The Gachibowli police subsequently brought him to Hyderabad and produced him before a magistrate, who remanded him to judicial custody on Sunday. Gurjar was arrested at Mumbai airport on Sunday and was sent to 14 days of judicial remand based on a complaint filed by a 29-year-old woman. Gachibowli police had registered the case on August 15 charging him with the offence of having sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means. The woman, according to her complaint, first became acquainted with Gurjar through Instagram in 2021. Their conversations subsequently moved to WhatsApp, and they developed a relationship. She alleged that they met in person for the first time on December 25, 2021. According to the complaint, Gurjar subsequently promised to marry her and assured her that she would have rights equivalent to those of a wife. The woman also alleged that Gurjar persuaded her to quit her job in the United States after promising that they would start a business together. She added that the alleged harassment subsequently affected her ability to concentrate on her work. She also alleged that Gurjar would distance himself and block her phone number whenever she questioned him about marriage. The woman further alleged that she and Gurjar lived together while she was in the US and continued living together after she returned to India. Gurjar reportedly stayed with her from October 2025 to March 2026. She alleged that they subsequently continued living together in Hyderabad before he left without informing her. Based on the complaint, Gachibowli police registered a case and began investigating the allegations. Gurjar, 42, is known for his roles in television and films as well as his professional wrestling career. He made his acting debut as Bhima in Star Plus’ Mahabharat , which aired from 2013 to 2014. He later appeared in Sankatmochan Mahabali Hanuman and made his professional wrestling debut with WWE as ‘Sanga’ after appearing for tryouts in Dubai in 2017.

items.title: Landslide and flash flood wreak havoc in Kerala: 4 dead, 4 missing
items.summary: Four people died and four others went missing after a landslide and flash flood hit separate locations in Kerala’s Idukki and Malappuram respectively on Sunday, September 20. In Idukki, two people were killed and one person seriously injured when a mudslide swept away a temporary shed at a garlic farm in Kottakkamboor near Munnar’s Vattavada at around 3 pm. The deceased have been identified as Kottakkamboor residents Balakrishnan, 50, and his sister Chinnu, 35. Balakrishnan’s wife Mariyamma, 40, was seriously injured and is undergoing treatment at the Munnar Government Hospital. The three were working at the farm when heavy rain began. They took shelter in a temporary shed, which was struck by the landslide and carried away by the debris. Local residents rescued the three, but Balakrishnan and Chinnu died at the spot. Devikulam Subcollector V M Arya said torrential rain was believed to have triggered the landslide. An electric pole also fell onto the shed during the incident, and authorities are examining whether electrocution contributed to the deaths. The exact cause will be known after the post-mortem examinations. The bodies have been taken to Adimaly Taluk Hospital for post-mortem. As the incident occurred in a remote part of Kottakkamboor, rescue workers had to use bamboo stretchers to carry the victims. Meanwhile, in Malappuram, two people died after a flash flood swept through the Kottapuzha river at TK Colony near Pookkottumpadam at around 5.30 pm on Sunday. Four others are still missing. The deceased have been identified as Tirur native Parannaparamban Muhammad Kutty, 65, and Mangadan Anas, 26, of Edarikode. Anas was working as a private bus employee. Those missing are Karuvarakundu native Rahim, 35, Wandoor Kottakkunnu native Kuppanath Sajjad, Chettiyarammal Kuruppath Rafeeque, 41, and Sajitha, 26, a resident of TK Colony. Sajitha was reportedly washing clothes at a riverbank when she was swept away. The flash flood occurred after heavy rain in the forested areas upstream, even though there had reportedly been little rain around the location. A large number of people were at different spots along the Kottapuzha river, a popular destination for visitors, when the water level rose suddenly. A joint search involving the National Disaster Response Force, Fire and Rescue Services and local residents resumed at 6.30 am on Monday after operations were suspended overnight because of the strong current.
